normalization.coefficient_definition: g[n] = coefficient of w^(n+1) in G

routes.objective: Prove two canonical quotient identities for every d >= 2.
obligations: Prove x1^(3d-3) - lambda[d]*Delta[d] belongs to I[d] for every d>=2.
Prove x3^(d-1) - nu[d]*Delta[d] belongs to I[d] for every d>=2.
Prove lambda[d] and nu[d] are nonzero for every d>=2.
Connect the identities to the distinguished inverse-series initial state; a recurrence valid only off an exceptional branch is insufficient.
falsifiers: An exact degree d where either canonical socle monomial is zero while Delta[d] is nonzero in the quotient.
A proof that one required scalar vanishes for some d.

routes.objective: Construct a finite set of primes whose product automaton supplies a same-prime GOOD fibre for every d.
obligations: Give exact Cartier or section transitions for the coefficient array of G over each selected prime.
Lift coefficient states to a finite, fail-closed ideal certificate such as a bounded Groebner signature or explicit pure-power identities.
Prove that every reachable product state has at least one GOOD prime component.
Keep all projective strata for one degree inside one prime-labelled certificate.

known_obstruction.statement: For p>=7, g[n]=0 mod p if n=-k mod p and 2<=k<=floor((p+2)/4).
known_obstruction.consequence: Every fixed prime has infinitely many BAD windows; a one-prime automaton cannot solve the challenge.

finite_evidence.claim_boundary: observed through d=300 only; not a universal cover

falsifiers: A reachable product state that is BAD at every proposed prime.
A transition certificate that checks rational points only rather than geometric points over the algebraic closure.
A certificate assembled from different primes on different projective strata.

routes.objective: Explain why the distinguished inverse-series solution cannot occupy Furter's exceptional recurrence mode.
obligations: Use the global initial state or a new invariant; universal pole-branch recurrences alone retain the exceptional factor.
Derive an all-degree conclusion for the actual inverse-coefficient sequence, not for generic recurrence solutions.
falsifiers: A purported desingularization that only divides by the exceptional factor without proving compatibility at its zero.
An argument that assumes the wanted nonvanishing at the exceptional index.

universal_solution: A human-checkable proof of radical(I[d])=(x1,x2,x3) for every d>=2.
Every computer-generated finite object in the proof has an exact checker and a frozen manifest.
No floating-point or probabilistic acceptance path is proof-critical.
The index and consequence dictionary is checked directly against Furter and LPS.
valuable_partial_result: A proved all-degree theorem closing one obligation above.
A rigorously excluded structural route with explicit ansatz bounds.
Portable exact certificates extending the finite benchmark beyond d=300.
